sections.title: Fats
sections.narration: 5 grams of fat. Cholesterol is 13 milligrams, so the cholesterol row stays controlled. Saturated fat is 2.4 grams, a moderate tradeoff rather than a huge problem. Polyunsaturated fat is only 0.2 grams, so this is not where the useful fats come from. For dairy, fat quality can help, but it can also drag the entry down.

sections.title: Proteins
sections.narration: 9 grams of protein. That clears the useful-protein gate, but the amount is still moderate rather than huge. Essential amino acids score is 7 out of 9, and bioavailability is 90%, so the quality side is much stronger than the amount. For dairy, useful protein is one of the main reasons it works.

sections.title: Vitamins
sections.narration: Vitamin B12 is 31% daily value, the clear vitamin strength. Vitamin A is only 2% daily value, so there is not much backup vitamin support. For dairy, B12 helps a lot, but this is not a broad vitamin win.

sections.title: Minerals
sections.narration: Calcium is 8% daily value, the best mineral number but still too low to carry the section. Zinc is 5% daily value, and magnesium is 3% daily value, so the backup minerals are light too. For dairy, calcium is the obvious mineral check, and here it is not high enough.

sections.title: Pros
sections.narration: Pros first: fermented-food angle adds extra value. Plain Greek yogurt can bring live-culture context that plain milk does not. Thick texture helps satiety. The strained texture makes it more filling than many softer dairy options. Helps make meals feel complete. It works as a simple base for breakfasts, bowls, sauces, or snacks.

sections.title: Cons
sections.narration: Cons next: dairy tolerance can be a barrier. Lactose sensitivity or dairy avoidance can make it a poor fit for some people. Sweetened versions change the profile fast. The plain record is strong, but common flavoured tubs can add a lot of sugar. Format choices can drag it down fast. The exact tub and how it is used matter a lot.
